title: Smooth fixed subgroup for roots of unity in a multiplicative group action
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $n\geq1$ an integer. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme over $S$ [def-pc-scheme] with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Let $H$ be a smooth affine $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Put $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}R[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units, and $\mu_{n,S}=\operatorname{Spec}R[z]/(z^n-1)$ with the induced group law. Let $a:\mathbf G_{m,S}\times_SH\to H$ be an action by group automorphisms: after every commutative $R$-algebra extension it satisfies $a(1,h)=h$, $a(tu,h)=a(t,a(u,h))$, and $a(t,hh')=a(t,h)a(t,h')$. For an $R$-algebra $B$, define
$$F(B)=\{h\in H(B):a(v,h_{B'})=h_{B'}\text{ for every commutative }B\text{-algebra }B'\text{ and every }v\in(B')^\times\text{ with }v^n=1\}.$$
Then $F$ is represented by a closed subgroup scheme $F\hookrightarrow H$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $F\to S$ is smooth and of finite presentation. For every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$, the closed subgroup $F\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R'$ [def-pc-base-change] represents the same fixed-point functor for $H_{R'}$ and $\mu_{n,R'}$. No invertibility of $n$, reducedness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 2.2.4, printed pp.64–66, and the semidirect-product argument of Example 2.2.6, printed pp.66–67, applied to H semidirect G_m and its subgroup mu_n; used explicitly in the proof of Lemma 4.2.2, printed p.118. The base-change assertion is the functorial fixed-subgroup construction. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative group-scheme theorem.

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-sfb-gm-affine-action-grading] the given action supplies $C=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbf Z}C_k$, with $R$ and $1$ in degree zero, $C_kC_l\subseteq C_{k+l}$ and $a(t,x)(c_k)=t^kx(c_k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], applied to the whole affine source and target, $C$ is finitely presented over $R$. Regroup the finite decompositions by residue classes modulo $n$: $C=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}E_r$, where $E_r=\bigoplus_{k\equiv r\pmod n}C_k$. Products satisfy $E_rE_s\subseteq E_{r+s}$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine. The finite presentation input is Morphisms Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize.

proof.text:
For an $R$-algebra $B$ and $x:C	o B$, test fixedness on $B'=B[u]/(u^n-1)$ at the class of $u$, which is a unit with inverse $u^{n-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $1,u,\ldots,u^{n-1}$ form a $B$-basis. For $c_k\in C_k$, the formula of [lem-sfb-gm-affine-action-grading] becomes $(u^r-1)x(c_k)=0$, where $0\leq r<n$ is the residue of $k$. If $r
e0$, the coefficient of $u^r$ is $x(c_k)$, hence it is zero. Conversely, if $x(C_k)=0$ whenever $n
mid k$, then after every $B$-algebra extension and for every $v$ with $v^n=1$, the same formula gives $a(v,x)(c_k)=x(c_k)$: either $x(c_k)=0$ or $v^k=1$. Finite additivity proves fixedness on all $C$. Thus fixedness is equivalent to $x(E_r)=0$ for all $r
e0$.

source.place: Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, homogeneous action formula; the universal-root coefficient test is agent-written, using the monic quotient basis recorded in Algebra Tag 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian, proof of (10) implies (1).

proof.text: Let $I\subseteq C$ be the ideal generated by all $E_r$ with $r\ne0$, and put $D=C/I$. The preceding criterion gives, naturally in $B$, $F(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(D,B)$. The affine correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] therefore shows that $F=\operatorname{Spec}D$ represents the required functor. The quotient map $C\twoheadrightarrow D$ gives a closed immersion into $H$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This constructs the scheme from the explicit ideal, without assuming a fixed-point representability theorem.

source.place: Agent construction from the grading in Tag 0EKK; quotient spectra are closed immersions by Schemes Tag 01IG, example-closed-immersion-affines, and Morphisms Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, (1)<=>(2).

proof.text: The fixed points are closed under multiplication and inverse and contain the identity on every test algebra, since the action is by group automorphisms. These operations are morphisms on $\operatorname{Spec}D$: use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] to write $F\times_SF=\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_RD)$. The universal two points, from $d\mapsto d\otimes1$ and $d\mapsto1\otimes d$, are fixed by step 2. Their product in $H(D\otimes_RD)$ is fixed and hence its coordinate map kills $I$. It factors as $D\to D\otimes_RD$, defining multiplication by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The inverse of the universal point over $D$ similarly defines $D\to D$, and the identity over $R$ defines $D\to R$. All group identities follow from those in $H$, since $F(B)\hookrightarrow H(B)$ is injective for every $B$. Thus the constructed closed subscheme is a subgroup over the arbitrary base $S$.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; elementary factorization of the universal group points through the explicit quotient.

proof.text: Choose finitely many algebra generators of $C$ using its finite presentation. Replace them by all their integer-homogeneous components; this is still a finite generating set, since its generated algebra contains the original generators. Let $K$ be the ideal generated by those members whose degrees are not divisible by $n$. Certainly $K\subseteq I$. Conversely express any $c\in C_k$ with $n\nmid k$ as a polynomial in the homogeneous generators. Project this equality onto residue degree $\overline{k}$; every remaining monomial has a factor of nonzero residue degree, because a product of degree-zero-residue factors has degree-zero residue. Thus $c\in K$. Hence $I=K$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal] to conclude that $D$ is finitely presented over $R$.

source.place: Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type, and the presentation obtained by adjoining finitely many ideal generators. Finite homogeneous generation and the residue projection argument are elementary consequences of the grading.

proof.text: To check the square-zero lifting property for $D$, let $B$ be any commutative $R$-algebra, $J\subseteq B$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:B\to B/J$ its quotient map, and $g:D\to B/J$ an $R$-algebra map. The composite $\bar g:C\to D\to B/J$ kills $E_r$ for $r\ne0$. The smoothness of $H\to S$ gives smoothness of $R\to C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] to obtain an $R$-algebra map $f:C\to B$ lifting $\bar g$. For $r\ne0$ we have $f(E_r)\subseteq J$.

source.place: Tag 02H4, lemma-affine-formally-smooth, and Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth; ordinary square-zero lifting is Algebra Tag 031J, proposition-characterize-formally-smooth.

proof.text:
Define $h:C	o B$ by $h(\sum_r c_r)=f(c_0)$ for $c_r\in E_r$. It is additive, $R$-linear and sends $1$ to $1$. Check multiplication on $a\in E_r$, $b\in E_s$. If $r=s=0$, multiplicativity is that of $f$. If $r+s
e0$, then $h(ab)=0=h(a)h(b)$. If $r+s=0$ and $r
e0$, then also $s
e0$, so $h(ab)=f(ab)=f(a)f(b)=0$ by $f(E_r),f(E_s)\subseteq J$ and $J^2=0$, and again $h(a)h(b)=0$. Expanding finite sums proves multiplicativity for all $a,b$. Thus $h$ is an $R$-algebra map. It kills $E_r$ for $r
e0$, hence kills $I$, and descends to $\widetilde g:D	o B$. Finally $qh(c)= ar g(c_0)= ar g(c)$, so $q\widetilde g=g$. No division by $n$ occurs.

source.place: Agent square-zero projection calculation using the grading of Tag 0EKK. This extends the same explicit weight-zero projection calculation used for the multiplicative-group fixed lifting lemma to residue weights modulo n.

proof.text: Step 7 proves exactly the square-zero lifting hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-fp-square-zero-lifting-smooth-ring-map] for the finitely presented algebra $D$ of step 5. Hence $R\to D$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $F\to S$ is smooth as a scheme morphism. Its global finite presentation follows from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]: its source and target are affine and its finite algebra presentation in step 5 gives local finite presentation on the whole affine chart, in the sense of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 00TN, proposition-smooth-formally-smooth; affine comparison More on Morphisms Tags 02H4 and 02H6. Finite presentation uses Morphisms Tag 01TP and the affine-source qcqs consequence recorded in the cited permanence node.

proof.text: Let $R\to R'$ be arbitrary and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$. By [def-pc-base-change] and the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product], the $B$-points of $F\times_SS'$ over $S'$ are $F(B)$ for every commutative $R'$-algebra $B$, and $H_{R'}(B)=H(B)$. The induced action is the original one on these points, and $\mu_{n,R'}(B')=\{v\in(B')^\times:v^n=1\}$. Every commutative $B$-algebra $B'$ automatically has the unique compatible $R'$-structure induced through $B$. Thus both fixedness conditions quantify over exactly the same $B'$ and $v$ and impose exactly the same equations. This proves the required representation after base change, with its inclusion in $H_{R'}$. The closed immersion assertion can also be seen directly from its coordinate quotient: by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $(C/I)\otimes_RR'$ is the quotient of $C\otimes_RR'$ by the ideal generated by the image of $I$ (the mutually inverse maps send $(c+I)\otimes r'$ to the class of $c\otimes r'$). Hence its inclusion is closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion], with no flatness requirement on $R'$.
